newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 5.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
U.S. President Bill Clinton on Tuesday praised the efforts of Sheikh Hasina's government for consolidating democracy in Bangladesh.
World Health Organisation (WHO) representative in Dhaka Dr Wit Hardjotanoj on Tuesday said arsenic contamination of sub-soil water in Bangladesh could be overcome through "carefully planned actions."
Some 459 Burmese Rohingya refugees returned home on Tuesday, taking the total number of repatriated refugees to 2,23,450.
Commerce and Industries Minister Tofael Ahmed on Tuesday dismissed apprehensions of fertiliser shortfall during the current crop season.
The European Union has agreed to continue the Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) for Bangladeshi knitwear export for the next three years, Commerce and Industries Minister Toafel Ahmed said.
Seven peopl were killed and 50 others injured in a fatal bus accident on the Dhaka-Sylhet highway on Tuesday.

An expert team, sponsored by the Asian Development Bank (ADB), was looking into the whole gamut of the country's capital market to help its development, Finance Minister S A M S Kibria said on Tuesday.

Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) Secretary General Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan on Tuesday reiterated his party's firm stance against import of electricity from India, saying the power shortfall should be overcome by raising domestic generation capacity.
